questions.q: Diarrhoea before and during the menses, with the menstrual flow only at night or early morning, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Bovista (Boericke): diarrhoea before and during menses; flow only at night or early in the morning.

questions.q: Euthanasia (passive) in India was permitted with safeguards following the Supreme Court judgment in:
opts: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018)
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Also recognised living wills.

questions.q: A screening test gives: true positives 80, false negatives 20, false positives 30, true negatives 870. Its sensitivity is:
questions.why: Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN) = 80/100 = 80%. 72.7% is the PPV, 96.7% the specificity and 97.8% the NPV.

questions.q: Called the 'homoeopathic knife' for its power to hasten suppuration in whitlow and abscess, the remedy is:
questions.why: Myristica sebifera hastens suppuration and is often said to shorten the course of panaritium.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's first repertory, published in 1832, dealt with:
questions.why: 'Systematic Alphabetic Repertory of the Antipsoric Medicines' (1832); the non-antipsorics followed in 1835.

questions.q: Which repertory follows Kent's plan but is arranged with chapters in alphabetical order?
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Robin Murphy's repertory lists chapters alphabetically.

questions.q: In Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab (2005), the Supreme Court held that to prosecute a doctor for criminal negligence:
opts: any error of judgement is enough
the negligence must be gross or reckless, and a private complaint should be supported by a credible medical opinion
the patient's consent form must be produced first
only a civil suit for compensation is permitted
questions.why: The judgment set guidelines protecting doctors from frivolous criminal prosecution: simple lack of care is civil; criminal liability needs gross negligence.

questions.q: In posterior dislocation of the hip, the limb is held in:
questions.why: Posterior dislocation (dashboard injury) gives flexion, adduction and internal rotation, and may injure the sciatic nerve.

questions.q: According to §159, the smaller the dose of the homoeopathic remedy:
opts: the smaller and shorter is the homoeopathic aggravation
the longer the remedy must be repeated
the greater the risk of new symptoms
questions.why: §159: the smaller the dose, the smaller and shorter the apparent increase of the disease in the first hours.

questions.q: Retention of flatus with distension after abdominal operations, with no passage of gas up or down, calls for:
questions.why: Raphanus is the noted remedy for postoperative gas retention.
